{"content": "Below is a concise guide on how to create a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that is configured with a **GPU** (the closest available to an RTX A6000 is the NVIDIA Tesla A100) and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

---

## 1. Prerequisites

| Item | How to set it up |
|------|------------------|
| **Project** | Create a project in the Google Cloud Console or use an existing one. |
| **Billing** | Enable billing for the project. |
| **Compute Engine API** | Enable the Compute Engine API (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`). |
| **GPU quota** | Request a GPU quota for the region you plan to use (e.g., `us-central1`). |
| **OAuth token** | For REST calls, obtain an OAuth 2.0 access token with the scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`. |

---

## 2. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Set variables
PROJECT=my-gcp-project
ZONE=us-central1-a
INSTANCE_NAME=my-gpu-instance
MACHINE_TYPE=n1-standard-8   # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM
GPU_TYPE=nvidia-tesla-a100   # closest to RTX A6000
GPU_COUNT=1
IMAGE_PROJECT=ubuntu-os-cloud
IMAGE_FAMILY=ubuntu-2004-lts

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create $INSTANCE_NAME \
  --project=$PROJECT \
  --zone=$ZONE \
  --machine-type=$MACHINE_TYPE \
  --accelerator=type=$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT \
  --image-project=$IMAGE_PROJECT \
  --image-family=$IMAGE_FAMILY \
  --boot-disk-size=50GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

> **Note:** The `--maintenance-policy=MIGRATE` flag ensures that the instance can be live‑migrated during maintenance windows.

---

## 3. Using the REST API

### 3.1 Endpoint

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances
```

### 3.2 Request Body (JSON)

```json
{
  "name": "my-gpu-instance",
  "machineType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 50,
        "diskType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100"
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "automaticRestart": true,
    "onHostMaintenance": "MIGRATE"
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

### 3.3 Example cURL Command

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/instances"
```

Replace `@instance.json` with the path to a file containing the JSON body above.

---

## 4. Why RTX A6000 isn’t directly available

Google Cloud’s GPU catalog currently includes models such as:

- NVIDIA Tesla T4
- NVIDIA Tesla P4
- NVIDIA Tesla P100
- NVIDIA Tesla V100
- NVIDIA Tesla A100
- NVIDIA Tesla A30
- NVIDIA Tesla A10

The **RTX A6000** is a consumer‑grade GPU and is not part of the Compute Engine GPU offerings. The **Tesla A100** is the closest high‑performance GPU available for general‑purpose workloads.

---

## 5. Next Steps

1. **Verify GPU availability** in your chosen zone via the Cloud Console or `gcloud compute accelerator-types list`. |
2. **Attach additional disks** if you need more storage. |
3. **Set up firewall rules** to allow SSH (port 22) or other required ports. |
4. **Install NVIDIA drivers** on the instance after boot (if not automatically installed). |

---

**Happy computing!**
", "filename": "create-gcp-gpu-instance.md"}
